_about: Reviewed changes to the Factbook government type, independence and former names. 'type' and 'note' replace the government type. Under 'independence', 'pick' chooses one of the Factbook dates, and 'label', 'date' and 'description' replace parts of the record. 'former' replaces the list of former names. 'reason' explains each change.

AFG.note: The Taliban took power in August 2021. Most countries do not recognize the government.
AFG.reason: The Factbook note gives only the position of the United States.

AND.note: The President of France and the Bishop of Urgell are the heads of state.
AND.reason: The Factbook text is a long sentence.

ATA.note: The treaty limits the continent to peaceful and scientific use and sets aside territorial claims.
ATA.reason: The Factbook text is a long sentence.

BFA.note: The army has ruled since the two coups of 2022.
BFA.reason: The Factbook gives the form in the constitution.

CYP.note: Northern Cyprus, which only Turkey recognizes, is a parliamentary republic.
CYP.reason: The Factbook gives two types in one sentence.

ESH.note: Morocco controls most of the territory. The Polisario Front claims it as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic.
ESH.reason: The Factbook text is a long sentence.

GNB.note: The army took power in November 2025.
GNB.reason: The Factbook gives the form in the constitution.

MDG.note: The army took power in October 2025.
MDG.reason: The Factbook gives the form in the constitution.

MLI.note: The army has ruled since the coups of 2020 and 2021.
MLI.reason: The Factbook gives the form in the constitution.

MMR.note: The army took power in February 2021.

NER.note: The army has ruled since the coup of July 2023.

PSE.note: The Palestinian Authority administers parts of the West Bank.
PSE.reason: The Factbook has no entry for Palestine.

SDN.note: The army and the Rapid Support Forces have fought a civil war since April 2023.
SDN.reason: The Factbook gives the form in the constitution.

AUT.reason: The Factbook gives no official date. The First Republic is the start of the present state.

COK.label: Self-government
COK.reason: The Cook Islands are in free association with New Zealand.

ESH.label: Independence
ESH.description: The Polisario Front proclaimed the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic on 27 February 1976.
ESH.reason: The Factbook has no independence field for Western Sahara.

ETH.label: Founded
ETH.description: The Aksumite Kingdom. Ethiopia is the oldest independent country in Africa.
ETH.reason: The Factbook gives a sentence without a date.

FRA.reason: The Factbook gives no official date. Western Francia is the usual starting point of France.

GBR.reason: The Factbook gives no official date. The Acts of Union created the United Kingdom.

GNB.label: Independence
GNB.description: Declared. Portugal recognized it on 10 September 1974.
GNB.reason: The Factbook gives only the word declared.

JPN.reason: The Factbook's first date is the current constitution, not the founding.

NIU.label: Self-government
NIU.reason: Niue is in free association with New Zealand.

PSE.label: Independence
PSE.description: Declared by the Palestine National Council
PSE.reason: The Factbook has no entry for Palestine.

ROU.label: Independence
ROU.reason: The Factbook text has a parenthesis that does not close.

SOM.label: Independence
SOM.description: British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland united as the Somali Republic.
SOM.reason: The Factbook gives a long clause.

SPM.reason: The Factbook text repeats the word collectivity.

TWN.label: Founded
TWN.description: The Republic of China was established. Its government moved to Taiwan in 1949.
TWN.reason: The Factbook has no independence field for Taiwan.

names: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
FSM.reason: The Factbook list includes district names.

MAR.reason: Ifni, Spanish Sahara and Western Sahara are names of territories, not of Morocco.

names: Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma
MMR.reason: The country took the name Myanmar in 1989. The Factbook still uses Burma, so its list leaves it out.

WLF.reason: The Factbook gives a sentence: the Hoorn Islands is the former name of the Futuna Islands.

YEM.reason: The two states that united in 1990.
